report.summary: ride-hailing mobility platforms, sector improving. The most recent peer signals are broadly positive: Uber grew Q2 2026 gross bookings 22% year over year with a 13.3% margin (though its net debt rose sharply), Bolt posted its first-ever annual profit in 2025 and beat Kenya's government in court over commission caps, and DiDi swung back to a Q2 2026 quarterly profit after a Q1 loss. Remaining negatives are mostly unit- or market-specific: Uber's rising net debt, DiDi's first-half loss from overseas expansion, and the near-wipeout of Bolt's UK profit on legal costs. With no score move reported for Cabify this month, its static 50/100 looks company-specific rather than a reflection of sector-wide deterioration, since the peer group is if anything improving.
findings: Bolt: Bolt defeated the Kenyan government in court over commission caps and licence rules, easing regulatory pressure on its take rate in that market. [seen 2026-09-15, helps]
Uber: Uber's margin improved year over year to 13.3% in Q2 2026. [seen 2026-09-11, helps]
Uber: Uber's net debt rose sharply sequentially, offsetting its year-over-year improvement in revenue, EPS and pre-tax margin. [seen 2026-09-11, hurts]
Uber: Uber announced organizational changes removing management layers and simplifying team structures to refocus people and investments. [seen 2026-09-08, neutral]
DiDi: Didi returned to a net profit of 869 million yuan in Q2 2026, swinging to profit from a year earlier. [seen 2026-08-14, helps]
DiDi: Didi remained in the red for the first half of 2026 as aggressive overseas expansion weighed on results. [seen 2026-08-14, hurts]

Uber: Uber's Q2 2026 gross bookings grew 22% year over year on a constant-currency basis with trips up 18%, GAAP income from operations of $1.9 billion and non-GAAP operating income of $2.1 billion, up 40% year over year. [seen 2026-08-05, helps]
Bolt: Bolt posted its first-ever net profit of €900,000 for 2025, with revenue up 14% year over year to €2.27 billion. [seen 2026-06-29, helps]
DiDi: Didi swung to a Q1 2026 net loss of 1.2 billion yuan ($177.43 million) as higher losses from its international business weighed on profitability. [seen 2026-06-02, hurts]
Bolt: Bolt's UK arm reported a pre-tax profit of £133,355 for 2024, down from £8.2 million in 2023, as ongoing legal battles consumed considerable resources. [seen 2025-09-18, hurts]
FreeNow: Lyft agreed to acquire European taxi app FreeNow for $199 million, its first acquisition in the highly competitive European ride-hailing market. [seen 2025-04-16, neutral]
